r0.why: Natural volcanic glass from rapidly cooled extruded lava with minimal crystal growth [1]; felsic, rich in listed light elements [2]; margins of rhyolitic obsidian flows [3].

r1.why: High silica gives high viscosity [4]; viscosity inhibits diffusion and nucleation [5]; with rapid cooling gives natural glass [6].

r2.why: Not a true mineral, non-crystalline and too variable [14]; mineraloid [15]; dark yet extremely felsic [16]; 70% or more SiO2 plus other oxides [17]; granite and rhyolite [18].

r3.why: Hard, brittle, amorphous so sharp edges [7]; experimental scalpel blades [8]; knapping like flint [43]; conchoidal fracture like all glass [44]; early mirrors [45].

r4.why: Kariandusi and Acheulian sites dated 700,000 BC with few objects [38]; Lipari bladelets and trade to Sicily, Po valley, Croatia [39]; Anatolian obsidian in Levant and Iraqi Kurdistan from about 12,500 BC [41].

r5.why: Metastable, devitrifies, so pre-Miocene obsidian rare [19]; water accelerates [21]; under 1% water when new, hydrates to perlite in groundwater [22].

r6.why: Usually dark, colour varies with impurities [23]; iron and transition elements give dark brown to black [24]; cristobalite spherulites make snowflake obsidian [27].
